title: Fits that ignore six tested SST offsets retain 14-15% of linear trend information under equal independent noise
abstract: We tested whether separate offsets at six tested SST input changes permit a feedback estimate without fixed step amplitudes. We used published monthly SST and five atmosphere-model response series for ice-free ocean at 60 S to 60 N. Under equal independent noise, the best unbiased linear slope that ignores these offsets retains 13.80% of trend information in 1982-2022 and 14.86% in 2001-2022. Minimum standard errors increase by factors of 2.69 and 2.59. Raw DOISST and two published corrections give the same fitted ratio within 3e-9 W m-2 K-1. But this agreement follows from the fit. The common fit raises the SST trend in all five raw products. It changes the 2001-2022 DOISST ratio from -1.650 to -1.197 W m-2 K-1. A smooth constructed series also changes slope without any offsets. Thus, offset immunity does not identify the ordinary trend of unrestricted climate evolution. The package gives the design bound, code, time weights, date checks, conditional uncertainty and retrieval instructions. No new SST observations are used. Serial dependence, model error, product error and a wrong common-trend model limit inference. The exact information bound applies only to the stated noise model.
